    def test_decoder_accuracy(metrics, submitted_data_full, submitted_data_stats, reference_data_stats):
        """Run the provided train_decoder.py script on the sample data and check that it runs without error."""
    
        train_params = {
            'npcs': 100,
            'lr': 1e-3,
            'l1_weight': 1e-4,
            'balanced_loss': True,
        }
    
        # train the decoder on the submitted data
        rng_state = reference_data_stats.get('rng_state', None)
        try:
            scores, predictions, pcs, confidences, train_idx, test_idx, model, output, _ = \
                train_validate_decoder(submitted_data_full['neural'], submitted_data_full['input'],
                                    submitted_data_full['output'], state=rng_state, **train_params)
        except torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError:
            print("CUDA out of memory error during decoder training. Retrying on CPU...")
            train_params['device'] = torch.device('cpu')
            scores, predictions, pcs, confidences, train_idx, test_idx, model, output, _ = \
                train_validate_decoder(submitted_data_full['neural'], submitted_data_full['input'],
                                    submitted_data_full['output'], state=rng_state, **train_params)

        }

        metrics['validation_balanced_accuracy_reference'] = ref_accuracy

        output_matches, output_costs = match_outputs_by_range_and_fractions(

            submitted_data_stats['output_fractions'],
            reference_data_stats['data_summary']['output_fractions'],
        )
    
        metrics['validation_balanced_accuracy_ratio'] = {
            ref_name: sub_accuracy[sub_name] / ref_accuracy[ref_name]
            for ref_name, sub_name, _ in output_matches
        }

Perform all of the following checks:\n   521→\n   522→**Check 1: Accuracy vs chance analysis**\n   523→- For each output, compare validation accuracy to chance (1/num_classes)\n   524→- Accuracy below chance indicates a bug, investigate and fix conversion issues to improve this. \n   525→- Accuracy below 1.5x chance may also indicate a bug, investigate whether changes in conversion logic could improve accuracy. \n   526→\n   527→**Check 2: Accuracy comparison to papers**\n   528→- Find every decoding accuracy reported in the reference papers\n   529→- Create a table comparing your accuracy to the papers' accuracy for each variable\n   530→- If your accuracy is lower than the reported accuracy, this may indicate a bug in your conversion that you must fix. \n   531→- Differences in algorithm/architecture should be relatively small because of the data dimensionality and size. Do not use this as an excuse to dismiss differences, investigate them completely before moving on. \n   532→\n   533→**Check 3: Train vs validation gap**\n   534→- If training accuracy is much higher (>1.5x) than validation accuracy for any output, investigate overfitting or data leakage. \n   535→\n   536→**If accuracy is low for an output, try these specific debugging steps:**\n   537→1. Check that processing of the data matches the reference code and papers. \n   542→\n   543→**Iteration protocol**: If ANY check above reveals an issue:\n   544→1. Include both the \"Go\" and \"Catch\" trials, but exclude the \"Aborted\" and \"Auto-rewarded\" trials.\n\n### Decoder Inputs:\n\nNo inputs for this task.\n\n### Decoder Outputs\n\n- Image identity (of the image presented during the non-grey screen), categorical variable. Time-varying.\n- Image change, binary variable. Have value of 1 right after a change in image identity, otherwise 0. Time-varying.\n- Running speed, discretized into five equal percentile bins. Time-varying.\n- Pupil diameter, discretized into five equal percentile bins.  Time-varying.\n- Trial outcome. Static per-trial.\n\n## Target Data Format\n\n- Save the full converted dataset to the pickle file `converted_data.pkl`.\n- All datasets must be converted into the following Python dictionary structure:\n\n```python\ndata = {\n    'neural': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\n    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\n\n    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\n    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\n        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\n    ] # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\n\n    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\n    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\n    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\n        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'metadata': {\n        'task_description': str, # They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. The AI uses the stimulus presentations' `is_change` flag rather than the trial-level `go` flag plus `change_time`.\n\n## 4-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Image change*?\n\ni. For each change stimulus presentation (where `is_change=True` and not omitted), a 750ms window from the change start time is marked as 1, otherwise 0.\n\nii.\n```python\nfor cs, ce in zip(change_starts, change_stops):\n    mask = (timepoints >= cs) & (timepoints < cs + 0.75)\n    change_signal[mask] = 1\nreturn change_signal\n```\n\niii. The 750ms window corresponds to one image presentation (250ms) plus gray inter-stimulus interval (500ms).\n\n## 4-c. How is `output` *Image change* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Image change is a binary variable (0 = no change, 1 = change). No thresholding is needed; it is directly computed as 0 or 1.\n\nii. See 4-b code.\n\niii. The binary nature is defined by the task specification.\n\n## 4-d. How is `output` *Image change* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. How is `output` *Running speed* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Running speed is discretized into 5 bins based on equal percentiles (0th, 20th, 40th, 60th, 80th, 100th percentiles). Bin edges are computed globally from all running speed data across all sessions. NaN values are assigned to bin 0.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_percentile_bins(values, n_bins=5):\n    valid = values[~np.isnan(values)]\n    percentiles = np.linspace(0, 100, n_bins + 1)\n    edges = np.percentile(valid, percentiles)\n    for i in range(1, len(edges)):\n        if edges[i] <= edges[i-1]:\n            edges[i] = edges[i-1] + 1e-10\n    return edges\n\ndef digitize_to_bins(values, bin_edges):\n    n_bins = len(bin_edges) - 1\n    binned = np.digitize(values, bin_edges[1:-1])\n    binned = np.clip(binned, 0, n_bins - 1)\n    binned[np.isnan(values)] = 0\n    return binned.astype(np.int64)\n```\n\niii. discretization levels for running / pupil\nPROJECT_CODE = 'VisualBehavior'\n\nTRIAL_OUTCOMES = ['hit', 'miss', 'false_alarm', 'correct_reject']\n\n\ndef get_cache(cache_dir):\n    return bpc.VisualBehaviorOphysProjectCache.from_s3_cache(cache_dir=cache_dir)\n\n\ndef extract_session_data(bc, session_experiments):\n    \"\"\"Load all planes for one session, merge neural data, resample behavior.\"\"\"\n    datasets = {}\n    for exp_id in session_experiments.index:\n        datasets[exp_id] = bc.get_behavior_ophys_experiment(exp_id)\n\n    ref_ds = list(datasets.values())[0]\n    ophys_ts = ref_ds.ophys_timestamps\n\n    # --- Neural: merge dF/F across planes ---\n    dff_list = []\n    plane_labels = []\n    for exp_id, ds in datasets.items():\n        dff_list.append(np.vstack(ds.dff_traces.dff.values))\n        area = session_experiments.loc[exp_id, 'targeted_structure']\n        depth = session_experiments.loc[exp_id, 'imaging_depth']\n        plane_labels.extend([f'{area}_{depth}um'] * len(ds.dff_traces))\n    neural_data = np.vstack(dff_list)  # --- Trials table ---\n    trials_table = ref_ds.trials\n\n    return {\n        'ophys_ts': ophys_ts,\n        'neural_data': neural_data,\n        'plane_labels': plane_labels,\n        'running_speed': running_speed,\n        'pupil_diameter': pupil_diameter,\n        'trials_table': trials_table,\n    }\n\n\ndef segment_trials(session_data):\n    \"\"\"Segment into trials using the built-in trials table.\n\n    For each non-aborted, non-auto-rewarded trial with a valid change_time,\n    extract ophys frames from start_time to stop_time (variable length).\n\n    Returns list of trial dicts with raw (continuous) running/pupil and\n    per-frame image identity and change indicator.\n    \"\"\"\n    ophys_ts = session_data['ophys_ts']\n    neural_data = session_data['neural_data']\n    running_speed = session_data['running_speed']\n    pupil_diameter = session_data['pupil_diameter']\n    trials_table = session_data['trials_table']\n    T = len(ophys_ts)\n\n    #
